details:
SAR2UAV is a prototype decision-support tool designed to identify probable flood-affected areas and prioritize UAV reconnaissance missions in Houston, Texas.

Problem: During flood emergencies, response teams need to identify affected locations quickly. Satellite observations can provide broad coverage, but converting those observations into actionable UAV reconnaissance priorities remains challenging.

Solution: SAR2UAV analyzes NASA-ISRO NISAR radar observations from August 26 and September 7, 2026, to identify probable flood-related backscatter changes. The workflow applies flood-candidate detection and cleaning, divides the study area into 25 geographic sectors, and combines flood severity with OpenStreetMap drivable-road exposure.

Methodology: Flood evidence determines whether a sector receives reconnaissance priority. Road exposure then modifies the relative priority among flood-affected sectors. The prototype uses 70% flood-severity weighting and 30% road-exposure weighting.

Results: The analysis identified approximately 1.40 km² of probable flood candidates, representing 0.035% of the study area. Sector D5 received the highest reconnaissance priority, followed by C5 and D4.

Technology: The project uses Python, geospatial data processing, NASA-ISRO NISAR radar observations, OpenStreetMap road data, and an interactive Streamlit dashboard. Users can adjust the priority weights and explore the resulting sector rankings.

Impact: SAR2UAV demonstrates how satellite observations and transportation-network information can support disaster-response planning by identifying locations for follow-up UAV reconnaissance.

Limitations: The detected flood areas are preliminary candidates rather than independently validated flood boundaries. The prototype supports reconnaissance planning and does not autonomously deploy or control UAVs.
